answer: Each seat holds one coppice row, and the guild photographs its willow bark at harvest. Every epoch the seed names one warp thread and a minute; the weaver shoots it beside a stamped reed. Graders count weft picks and read the weave's beat, which varies hand to hand like handwriting. Two seats sharing a row or a reed stamp merge into one vote and forfeit 40,000 POA each. Sixty rods cost $72 and three hours, so a thousand clones need three thousand hand hours, and no script can whisper a basket into being. A letter photocopies in a second; the hands that wove it take a lifetime to copy.
